newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- higher, but reluctantly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- higher, but reluctantly.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were higher in early trade Wednesday, but failed to get as much of a lift as Treasuries from unexpectedly good news on inflation.
One trader said he sensed muni cash prices were stuck almost at the same level as Tuesday, but said some issues were reluctantly up about 1/8 point.
"There's no sense of anybody going out there with the intent of lifting offerings," he said.
A second trader, who said prices were 1/4 higher, said activity was moving in a "sideways" direction. "There's just not a buzz," he said.
The Treasury market, in contrast, buzzed loudly when April producer price figures were released at 0830 EDT.
The index showed a 0.6 percent drop, instead of the unchanged reading economists had forecast. The core rate was down 0.1 percent, while expectations were for a 0.1 percent increase.
With analysts split over whether the Federal Reserve will again tighten interest rates at its May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, the PPI figure bolstered support for the no-move camp.
The government long bond moved 22/32 higher at 96-29/32, moving the yield down to 6.87 percent.
Debt futures also rallied. The June municipal contract was up 17/32 at 116-4/32, while June T-bonds gained 19/32 to 110-13/32. The MOB spread was 183 ticks.
Wednesday's municipal bond sales are expected to total $505 million in 22 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $267 million in 10 sales, with a $97 million New Hampshire Housing Development Authority deal through Merrill Lynch & Co. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 12 sales totaling $238 million are on the schedule. A $65 million Tennessee Housing Development Authority deal at 1030 EDT is the largest.
